Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 1) The commonest cause of obstructive jaundice in adults is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Common bile duct (CBD) stones are the leading cause of benign obstructive jaundice in adults.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 2) The most common type of gallstone is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Cholesterol stones account for approximately 75–80% of gallstones in Western populations.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 3) The most common symptom of gallstones is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Biliary colic is characterized by episodic right upper quadrant pain, often following fatty meals.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 4) Murphy’s sign is positive in:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Inspiratory arrest due to pain on palpation of the right upper quadrant is Murphy’s sign.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 5) The investigation of choice for suspected gallstones is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Ultrasound is highly sensitive for gallstones and is the initial imaging modality of choice.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 6) The gold standard treatment for symptomatic gallstones is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy is the standard treatment for symptomatic cholelithiasis.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 7) The commonest cause of acute pancreatitis is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Gallstones and alcohol are the two leading causes; gallstones are the most common overall in many surgical series.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 8) Serum amylase is most useful in diagnosing:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: A serum amylase level more than three times the upper limit of normal supports the diagnosis of acute pancreatitis.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 9) The most specific enzyme for acute pancreatitis is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Serum lipase is more specific than amylase and remains elevated for a longer duration.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 10) Cullen’s sign indicates:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Periumbilical ecchymosis (Cullen’s sign) may occur in severe hemorrhagic pancreatitis.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 11) Grey Turner’s sign is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Grey Turner’s sign represents retroperitoneal bleeding and is seen in severe acute pancreatitis.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 12) The most common malignant tumor of the pancreas is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: More than 90% of pancreatic cancers are ductal adenocarcinomas.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 13) Painless progressive obstructive jaundice is classically seen in:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: A painless enlarging jaundice with weight loss strongly suggests carcinoma of the pancreatic head.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 14) Courvoisier’s law is most commonly associated with:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: A palpable, non-tender gallbladder with jaundice suggests malignant biliary obstruction rather than gallstones.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 15) The investigation of choice for suspected CBD stones is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: MRCP is a non-invasive, highly accurate investigation for detecting common bile duct stones.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 16) ERCP is primarily indicated for:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: ERCP is mainly used for therapeutic interventions such as stone extraction and biliary stenting.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 17) The most common organism causing pyogenic liver abscess is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Klebsiella pneumoniae has become the leading cause of pyogenic liver abscess in many Asian countries.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 18) The treatment of amoebic liver abscess is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Metronidazole is highly effective against Entamoeba histolytica and is the first-line treatment.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 19) The most common benign tumor of the liver is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Cavernous hemangioma is the most common benign hepatic tumor and is usually asymptomatic.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 20) The most common primary malignant tumor of the liver is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Hepatocellular carcinoma is the commonest primary liver malignancy and is strongly associated with chronic hepatitis B, hepatitis C and cirrhosis.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 21) The most important risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma worldwide is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Chronic HBV infection is the leading global risk factor for HCC, especially in Asia and Africa.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 22) The tumor marker commonly elevated in hepatocellular carcinoma is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) supports the diagnosis and follow-up of hepatocellular carcinoma.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 23) Charcot’s triad consists of:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.option4: Fever, jaundice, right upper quadrant pain
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Charcot’s triad is characteristic of acute ascending cholangitis.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 24) Reynolds’ pentad includes Charcot’s triad plus:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Reynolds’ pentad indicates severe suppurative cholangitis requiring urgent biliary decompression.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 25) The treatment of acute ascending cholangitis includes:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Broad-spectrum antibiotics and biliary decompression (usually ERCP) are the cornerstones of treatment.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 26) Which imaging modality is most useful for staging pancreatic carcinoma?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Contrast-enhanced CT evaluates tumor size, vascular invasion and resectability.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 27) CA 19-9 is primarily used in:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: CA 19-9 is useful for monitoring pancreatic cancer but is not suitable for screening.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 28) The definitive operation for resectable carcinoma of the head of pancreas is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure) is the standard curative operation for tumors of the pancreatic head.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 29) The most common indication for splenectomy is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Traumatic splenic injury remains the commonest indication for splenectomy.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 30) Which organism is most strongly associated with overwhelming post-splenectomy infection (OPSI)?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Encapsulated organisms, particularly Streptococcus pneumoniae, are the major cause of OPSI.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 31) Patients undergoing elective splenectomy should receive vaccination against:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Vaccination against pneumococcus, meningococcus and Haemophilus influenzae type b is recommended before elective splenectomy.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 32) Kehr’s sign refers to:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.option2: Left shoulder pain due to diaphragmatic irritation
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Kehr’s sign suggests splenic injury with blood irritating the diaphragm.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 33) The most common benign lesion of the gallbladder is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Most gallbladder polyps are benign cholesterol polyps, especially when <10 mm.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 34) Which gallbladder polyp usually requires cholecystectomy?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Polyps ≥10 mm carry a higher risk of malignancy and are generally treated surgically.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 35) Mirizzi syndrome is caused by:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.option4: Impacted stone in the cystic duct or Hartmann’s pouch compressing the common hepatic duct
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: External compression of the common hepatic duct causes obstructive jaundice.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 36) The most common site of gallbladder carcinoma is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Gallbladder carcinoma most frequently arises in the fundus and is often associated with gallstones.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 37) Which condition is considered a premalignant lesion for gallbladder carcinoma?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Calcification of the gallbladder wall is associated with an increased risk of gallbladder carcinoma.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 38) The most common cause of splenomegaly worldwide is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: In tropical countries, malaria remains one of the leading causes of splenomegaly.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 39) The commonest cystic lesion following acute pancreatitis is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: A pancreatic pseudocyst develops after acute pancreatitis due to encapsulation of enzyme-rich fluid.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 40) A pancreatic pseudocyst persisting for more than 6 weeks and measuring more than 6 cm is generally managed by:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Persistent large symptomatic pseudocysts usually require drainage rather than conservative management.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 41) Which of the following is the most common cause of chronic pancreatitis?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Chronic alcohol consumption is the leading cause of chronic pancreatitis in adults.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 42) The most common symptom of chronic pancreatitis is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Persistent or recurrent epigastric pain radiating to the back is the hallmark of chronic pancreatitis.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 43) Pancreatic calcification on abdominal X-ray is characteristic of:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Pancreatic ductal calcification is a classic radiological feature of chronic pancreatitis.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 44) The most common endocrine tumor of the pancreas is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Insulinoma is the commonest functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor and usually presents with hypoglycemia.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 45) Whipple’s triad is seen in:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Whipple’s triad consists of hypoglycemic symptoms, low plasma glucose and relief after glucose administration.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 46) The commonest functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor causing peptic ulcer disease is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Gastrinoma causes Zollinger-Ellison syndrome due to excessive gastrin secretion.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 47) Which pancreatic tumor causes watery diarrhea, hypokalemia and achlorhydria?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: VIPoma classically causes WDHA syndrome (Watery Diarrhea, Hypokalemia, Achlorhydria).

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 48) Which pancreatic tumor is associated with necrolytic migratory erythema?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Glucagonoma commonly presents with diabetes, weight loss and necrolytic migratory erythema.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 49) Which imaging modality is the initial investigation of choice in suspected acute cholecystitis?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Ultrasound demonstrates gallstones, gallbladder wall thickening and pericholecystic fluid.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 50) The most common complication of gallstones is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Acute cholecystitis is the commonest complication resulting from cystic duct obstruction.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 51) Which of the following is the preferred treatment for acute calculous cholecystitis?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Early laparoscopic cholecystectomy during the same admission reduces complications and recurrence.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 52) The commonest site of impaction of a gallstone causing intestinal obstruction is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Gallstone ileus most commonly occurs at the narrow terminal ileum near the ileocecal valve.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 53) Rigler’s triad is seen in:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Rigler’s triad consists of intestinal obstruction, pneumobilia and an ectopic gallstone.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 54) The most common congenital cystic dilatation of the biliary tree is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Choledochal cysts predispose to recurrent cholangitis and cholangiocarcinoma.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 55) The investigation of choice for a choledochal cyst is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: MRCP accurately delineates the biliary anatomy and classifies choledochal cysts.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 56) The definitive treatment of a choledochal cyst is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Complete cyst excision minimizes the risk of recurrent cholangitis and malignancy.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 57) The commonest cause of portal hypertension worldwide is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Liver cirrhosis accounts for the majority of cases of portal hypertension.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 58) The most common site of variceal bleeding in portal hypertension is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Esophageal varices are the commonest and most clinically significant portosystemic collateral.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 59) The definitive treatment for hypersplenism secondary to portal hypertension is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.option3: Treatment of the underlying portal hypertension
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Management targets the underlying portal hypertension; splenectomy is reserved for selected cases.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 60) Which of the following is the most common indication for liver transplantation?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Decompensated cirrhosis is the most common indication for liver transplantation worldwide.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 61) The most common indication for ERCP is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: ERCP is primarily a therapeutic procedure used for CBD stone extraction and biliary stenting.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 62) Which of the following is a common complication of ERCP?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Post-ERCP pancreatitis is the most frequent complication of the procedure.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 63) The most common site of cholangiocarcinoma is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Perihilar (Klatskin) tumors are the commonest type of cholangiocarcinoma.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 64) Klatskin tumor arises at the:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.option4: Junction of right and left hepatic ducts
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: A Klatskin tumor is a hilar cholangiocarcinoma occurring at the hepatic duct confluence.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 65) Which congenital anomaly predisposes to cholangiocarcinoma?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Choledochal cysts significantly increase the lifetime risk of cholangiocarcinoma.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 66) The commonest cause of splenic rupture is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Blunt abdominal trauma is the leading cause of splenic rupture.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 67) A hemodynamically unstable patient with splenic rupture should undergo:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Unstable patients with ongoing hemorrhage require immediate operative management.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 68) The preferred management of a hemodynamically stable patient with low-grade splenic injury is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Most stable patients with low-grade splenic injuries are managed conservatively with close monitoring.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 69) Which vaccine should ideally be given before elective splenectomy?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Pneumococcal vaccination is essential before splenectomy; meningococcal and Hib vaccines are also recommended.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 70) Which of the following is the most common benign cyst of the liver?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Simple hepatic cysts are usually congenital, asymptomatic and discovered incidentally.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 71) Hydatid disease of the liver is caused by:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Hydatid cysts result from infection with the larval stage of Echinococcus granulosus.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 72) The investigation of choice for diagnosing a hydatid cyst is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Ultrasound is the initial imaging modality and often demonstrates daughter cysts and hydatid sand.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 73) Which drug is commonly used in the treatment of hydatid disease?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Albendazole is used before and after surgery or PAIR to reduce recurrence and sterilize the cyst.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 74) The most feared complication during hydatid cyst surgery is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Spillage of hydatid fluid may cause severe anaphylaxis and dissemination of daughter cysts.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 75) Which imaging modality is best for assessing pancreatic necrosis?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Contrast-enhanced CT is the standard imaging modality for detecting pancreatic necrosis.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 76) Which scoring system is commonly used to assess the severity of acute pancreatitis?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Ranson’s criteria help predict severity and mortality in acute pancreatitis.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 77) The initial management of acute pancreatitis includes:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Early fluid resuscitation, pain control and supportive care form the cornerstone of treatment.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 78) Which pancreatic complication usually develops several weeks after acute pancreatitis?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: A pseudocyst usually develops after approximately 4 weeks following acute pancreatitis.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 79) The most common cause of massive upper gastrointestinal bleeding in portal hypertension is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Esophageal varices are the most frequent source of life-threatening bleeding in portal hypertension.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 80) The definitive treatment for bleeding esophageal varices not controlled by endoscopic therapy is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: TIPS effectively decompresses the portal venous system when endoscopic and medical therapy fail.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 81) Which condition is the strongest risk factor for gallbladder carcinoma?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Gallstones are present in 70–90% of patients with gallbladder carcinoma, particularly large stones.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 82) Porcelain gallbladder is associated with an increased risk of:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Porcelain gallbladder is considered a premalignant condition and usually warrants cholecystectomy.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 83) The most common histological type of gallbladder carcinoma is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: More than 90% of gallbladder cancers are adenocarcinomas.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 84) Which investigation is most useful for staging gallbladder carcinoma?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Contrast CT evaluates local extension, lymph node involvement and distant metastases.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 85) Carcinoma of the gallbladder commonly spreads first to:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Direct invasion into the adjacent liver is common because of the thin gallbladder wall.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 86) Which of the following is a common cause of obstructive jaundice in children?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Choledochal cyst is an important congenital cause of obstructive jaundice in children.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 87) The most common site of pancreatic adenocarcinoma is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Approximately 60–70% of pancreatic adenocarcinomas arise in the head of the pancreas.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 88) A patient with pancreatic head carcinoma develops a palpable, non-tender gallbladder. This is known as:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: A palpable, distended gallbladder with painless jaundice suggests malignant biliary obstruction.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 89) The most common symptom of carcinoma of the pancreatic body and tail is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.option1: Epigastric pain radiating to the back
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Body and tail tumors often present late with back pain and weight loss rather than jaundice.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 90) Trousseau’s syndrome is classically associated with:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau’s syndrome) is a classic paraneoplastic manifestation of pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 91) Which of the following is the most common indication for distal pancreatectomy?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Distal pancreatectomy is performed for lesions involving the body and tail of the pancreas.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 92) Splenectomy is commonly performed along with distal pancreatectomy because:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.option3: Splenic vessels run along the pancreas
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: The splenic artery and vein closely adhere to the pancreatic body and tail, making splenic preservation difficult in many cases.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 93) Which blood investigation is most useful for monitoring hepatocellular carcinoma after treatment?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Serial AFP measurements help detect recurrence or response to therapy in many HCC patients.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 94) Which liver lesion has the greatest risk of spontaneous rupture?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Large hepatic adenomas, particularly in women taking oral contraceptives, may rupture and bleed.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 95) Which benign liver lesion usually requires no treatment?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Most hepatic hemangiomas are asymptomatic and are managed conservatively.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 96) The treatment of choice for pyogenic liver abscess is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Large or symptomatic pyogenic abscesses are managed with antibiotics and percutaneous drainage.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 97) The commonest organism causing emphysematous cholecystitis is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Gas-forming organisms, especially Clostridium spp., are commonly implicated in emphysematous cholecystitis.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 98) The commonest site of rupture of an amoebic liver abscess is into the:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: The right pleural cavity is the most common site of rupture because most abscesses occur in the right lobe.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 99) The commonest lobe involved in amoebic liver abscess is:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: The right hepatic lobe receives greater portal blood flow and is affected most frequently.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 100) Which complication of acute pancreatitis carries the highest mortality?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Infected pancreatic necrosis is a major cause of late mortality in severe acute pancreatitis.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 101) Which investigation best detects pancreatic duct abnormalities in chronic pancreatitis?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: MRCP provides excellent non-invasive visualization of the pancreatic ductal system.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 102) Which is the most common complication of chronic pancreatitis?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Progressive destruction of pancreatic islets commonly results in endocrine insufficiency and diabetes.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 103) Which of the following is the most common cause of death in pancreatic carcinoma?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Most patients present with advanced metastatic disease, which is the major cause of mortality.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 104) Following splenectomy, Howell-Jolly bodies may be seen in:
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Howell-Jolly bodies are nuclear remnants normally removed by the spleen; they appear after splenectomy or in functional asplenia.

Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.question: 105) Which statement regarding gallstone disease is correct ?
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.option1: ERCP is the investigation of choice for uncomplicated gallbladder stones.
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.option2: Ultrasonography is the first-line investigation for gallstones.
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.option3: Pigment stones are more common than cholesterol stones.
Hepatobiliary , Pancrease & Spleen.exp: Ultrasound is the initial investigation for suspected gallstones. Most asymptomatic stones are managed conservatively, and ERCP is reserved mainly for common bile duct stones.
